headline: Nvidia's beat fails to hold in Taipei while metals carry the Fed repricing

findings.headline: The AI sell-off is hitting the suppliers, not the platforms
findings.body: Nvidia closed lower after its beat on doubts over how long AI spending keeps climbing, and Taiwan took the hit: foreign investors have sold for three straight sessions, the Taiwan dollar is at its weakest in about 18 months and more than 200 listed and OTC stocks hit limit-down, led by memory, chip design and circuit-board makers. At the same time Anthropic raised about $81bn in the biggest IPO on record, so the AI trade is splitting between the platforms raising money and the hardware chain being sold. Japan held up far better, which points to a sector trade rather than a broad flight from Asia.

findings.headline: Metals are where the hike bets bite
findings.body: Gold sits near a 14-month low as the market leans toward further Fed hikes, a tilt last month's FOMC minutes reinforced. Copper's outsized drop pushed Anglo American and Glencore to the bottom of Europe's large caps, so the miners are taking rate pressure, not a growth scare.

sources.label: Bloomberg: Gold steadies near 14-month low as rate-hike pressure mounts

findings.headline: Nordic power squeeze is a supply story with a fix in sight
findings.body: Thursday's day-ahead prices jumped in every zone, the north included, because wind has dropped below normal for the time of year in recent days and nuclear availability is still well short of normal. Forsmark 3 is due back this morning and TenneT's limit on the German link into SE4 runs until tonight, so Friday's auction is the first test of whether the squeeze eases; hydro output near normal means there is no structural deficit behind it.

view: Our view: this is a valuation reset along the AI supply chain plus a firmer-Fed squeeze on metals, not a broad risk-off. Today's test is whether Europe's chip names follow; US jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey this afternoon, then Japan's CPI tonight, feed straight into the rate debate.
